Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Body, health & movement

bleary-eyed adjective

also with sore eyes, with inflamed eyes, rheumy-eyed, blear-eyed

classical

Plaut. Mil. 291b–292: Num tibi lippus videor?
Hor. Ep. 1.1.29: nōn tamen idcircō contemnās lippus inungī (Lewis & Short)

lippus, lippa, lippum

declension

with sore, running eyes

Horace’s proverb for common knowledge: known omnibus et lippīs et tōnsōribus (S. 1.7.3, Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Num tibi lippus videor? — Medicum istuc tibi meliust percontārier.

    Do my eyes look sore to you? — You’d better ask a doctor that.Plaut. Mil. 291b–292b

  • Lippī illīc oculī servos est simillimus.

    That slave is just like a sore eye.Plaut. Bacch. 913

See also eye, eye inflammation, one-eyed, blind.

SourcesLewis & Short: lippus

Plautus, Bacchides 913; Miles gloriosus 291b–292, 291b–292b.
